sequence.title: Guide the Clockwork Guardian
sequence.instructions: Give the guardian its commands in order. It performs exactly what you write, one line at a time.

reveal.title: Order of Instructions
reveal.explanation: A program is a list of instructions carried out from top to bottom. The guardian does not guess your intent — it only obeys the order. Change the order and you change the world.
reveal.world_analogy: A guardian walks the room exactly as a program walks down its lines.

variants.hint: The wall blocks the middle road. Walk the top lane, then come down.
Two turns are needed. Reach the right wall before you descend.

conditions.title: The Carved Door
conditions.instructions: Write ONE rule the door-keeper can follow. It must behave correctly in every situation it is shown.

reveal.title: Deciding With Conditions
reveal.explanation: A condition lets a program choose between two roads. The rule is written once, but it works for every situation — that is its power.
reveal.world_analogy: The door opens when the key is present, and searches when it is not.

variants.hint: Ask the door-keeper: does the traveller carry the key? Everything else follows.
Two questions are needed, in order: first the key, and only then the lantern.

loops.title: The Hollow River
loops.instructions: The tiles repeat. Compose as few blocks as possible — no more than the limit shown.

reveal.title: Repeating Without Repeating Yourself
reveal.explanation: A loop repeats work so you do not have to write it twice. Five identical tiles need one instruction and one number, not five lines.
reveal.world_analogy: The guardian crosses five identical tiles with one repeating command.

variants.hint: Five tiles. One block. The number is the trick.
Cross the tiles in one repeat, then turn once at the end.

code_assembly.title: The First Spell
code_assembly.instructions: Assemble the scroll. Choose the lines in the correct order to rebuild the spell.

reveal.title: Naming Things: Variables
reveal.explanation: A variable is a name that holds a value. Once named, you can use it again and again — change the value, and the whole spell changes.
reveal.world_analogy: Elarion keeps the tile count in a named chest instead of carving the number everywhere.

variants.hint: First name the number, then repeat it — and end with the indented action.
